summary: Discovery call where SignalBridge evaluated Redwood hosted quickstart (PLG credits, time-to-first-token) versus Dedicated/Private deployment for production. Main drivers: low time-to-prototype for product demos, eventual requirement for VPC/private deploy and KMS, cost sensitivity for high QPS inference, and measurable latency needs. Agreed next steps include pilot pricing, quickstart materials, and a technical kickoff week of 2026-04-27.
topics: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. With me are Samir and Maya from our solutions team. Could we do quick intros?
[00:08] Claire (SignalBridge, CTO): Claire here, CTO at SignalBridge. We build stream-analytics for telecom and have a roadmap to ship LLM-based summarization.
[00:15] Ethan (Lead ML): Ethan, ML eng, will own the integration and perf tests.
[00:18] Priya (Head of Security): Priya, security. I'll need to sign off on data flow and KMS requirements.
[00:22] Liam (Product): Liam, PM. We're looking at demo-ready features in 6 weeks.
[00:26] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is to understand your runway — do you want fastest path to prototype with our hosted API and free credits, or do you need to scope Dedicated/Private right away?
[00:36] Claire: Short answer: both. We want to prototype quickly for investor demo and internal testing, but long term we'll need a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for PII and compliance. We also care about latency — 95th percentile below 250ms for summarization ideally.
[00:50] Samir (SE): Helpful — couple clarifying q's. What's your expected query volume in prod? QPS and average tokens per request?
[00:58] Ethan: For initial pilot maybe 5-10 QPS, peak maybe 50 QPS. Typical prompt ~120 tokens, response ~200 tokens. But we may do heavy batching for nightly backfills.
[01:12] Maya: That volume maps well to our Hosted free-credits path for prototyping. You can be live in minutes. The Dedicated pool is better once you hit predictable sustained throughput and want isolated GPUs. Private gives VPC + customer KMS.
[01:28] Priya: On encryption: we need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and audit logs retained for 1 year. What's your stance?
[01:35] Jordan: We support KMS integrations and can surface audit logs; Private deployments offer the fullest control — for Hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit, but for CMK you would need Private or an Enterprise Dedicated config. We'll share SOC2 docs.
[01:48] Priya: Okay, send SOC2 + any ISO stuff. Also curious about network egress patterns: can data stay in our VPC?
[01:55] Samir: On Private, the control plane is separated and data flows stay in your VPC; on Dedicated we can do VPC peering or private endpoints depending on region. Hosted uses regional endpoints, and we have data residency options in EU/NA.
[02:08] Liam: For the prototype, how fast can we get to first token using your quickstart? We have limited dev cycles.
[02:15] Maya: Usually under an hour with our self-serve API and SDKs — sign-up, apply the free credits we allocate, pickup model from catalog, hit the generate endpoint. We have sample apps in Node/Python and a small benchmark script Samir will share.
[02:30] Ethan: When you say 'free credits', are those one-off, time-limited? Any throttling on the credit account?
[02:36] Jordan: We give a free credits allocation for PLG onboarding, typically usable over 30–90 days depending on the campaign. We can set up sandbox rate limits but usually it's generous enough for a proof-of-concept. For heavier tests we'll recommend a paid pilot or temporary reserved capacity.
[02:51] Claire: Cost is a big consideration. At scale, token costs matter — any levers to reduce per-token costs?
[02:57] Samir: Absolutely: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantized model variants. Redwood Optimize will recommend batch sizes and quant profiles based on your workload. For summarization we often use a quantized model variant that preserves LLM quality while lowering GPU memory and cost.
[03:14] Priya: Regarding SSO and RBAC — we need SAML SSO and role-based access controls before non-dev staff can access the console.
[03:21] Jordan: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported on our Enterprise tier (Dedicated/Private). RBAC is configurable per-route and per-token. We'll send the SSO setup guide.
[03:30] Claire: We might need to run internal perf tests against our own datasets. Can we run benchmarks that mimic our request sizes?
[03:35] Samir: Yes. We'll provide a small benchmark harness (curl + Python) that can replay your request distribution and measure latency and tokens. For more accurate results we can arrange a short abenchmark on Dedicated capacity or a private pilot with scheduled capacity.
[03:50] Ethan: A couple of technical specifics: how do you handle KV cache warming when models have long contexts? In our use case we have long customer transcripts and want efficient incremental summarization.
[03:59] Samir: We manage persistent KV caches for sessions on the serving runtime; you can pin model versions and use streaming responses. We also have prefix caching primitives that reduce repeated token cost for shared prompts. There might be some tokens to warm but it's significantly cheaper with caching enabled.
[04:16] Claire: Are there any limitations with streaming and tool-calls? We use tool invocations to hit internal APIs during generation.
[04:22] Maya: We support streaming and structured outputs; tool calling is supported. For Private, you can host connectors in your network. For hosted we proxy or you can make the tool call from your own infra using a webhook pattern.
[04:34] Priya: On compliance evidence — if you could share SOC2 Type II report and support SLA language that'd be useful.
[04:40] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 and the standard enterprise SLA. For Private/Dedicated we can talk about custom SLA addenda.
[04:47] Liam: Back to timeline — investor demo in six weeks. If we go quickstart hosted with credits, can we get a prototype by next week?
[04:54] Samir: Technically yes. Sign up, we'll allocate credits, share sample app, you can integrate in a day or two. To be safe plan ~3-5 working days for a polished demo including prompts and UI.
[05:06] Ethan: What about rollout strategy — if prototype looks good, how painful is migrating to Private or Dedicated later?
[05:12] Maya: We designed the API and config layer to be consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. You can pin model versions and move to a Dedicated pool or Private deployment with minimal code changes; mostly it's infra and networking work (VPC, keys). We'll help with a migration plan and can do a canary rollout.
[05:28] Claire: Pricing ask — can you ballpark pilot costs for Dedicated and Private? We need to present to finance.
[05:34] Jordan: I'll send ballpark numbers in a follow-up email: typical Dedicated reserved pools start at monthly commitments (we'll include GPU types and expected throughput). Private is higher — project-based license + infra + support. For now for the demo we'll focus on credits and pay-as-you-go hosted usage.
[05:50] Priya: One more question: data retention on Hosted for logs and raw prompts — do you retain user prompts by default? We need to ensure PII isn't retained in logs for Hosted trials.
[05:58] Jordan: By default, Hosted keeps logs for troubleshooting but you can opt-out or redact payloads; for full control use Private. We'll share the data handling doc.
[06:07] Claire: Great. I'd like to summarize next steps.
[06:10] Jordan: Summarize? Sure.
[06:12] Claire: 1) We'll do a hosted quickstart pilot using credits to build the investor demo; 2) Security will review SOC2 and KMS options; 3) If demo looks good, we'll scope Dedicated/Private for production and request pricing; 4) Schedule technical pilot kickoff week of 2026-04-27.
[06:29] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?
[06:32] Liam: No, sounds good.
[06:34] Priya: Please include contact for security follow-up.
[06:36] Jordan: I'll include Priya on the security docs email. Thanks everyone.
[06:40] (meeting ends)

Note: transcription includes occasional mislabels and small errors from auto-transcribe (eg 'KMS' sometimes appears as 'K M S', 'Redwood' occasionally 'Red wood'). Some speakers overlap briefly.
